children.text: name: cost-tracker-guide

description: Explains how the BIS AI Cost Tracker works (attribution, cost model, sync, data layout) and the conventions to follow when answering questions or changing code in this repository. Use for any question about attribution, AI credits, costs, LangSmith or GitHub sync.
# BIS AI Cost Tracker guide
## Architecture in one minute
- Copilot Chat in VS Code exports OpenTelemetry traces to LangSmith. `src/lib/sync` pulls them into SQLite (`data/app.db`) and also syncs GitHub issues and PRs.
- A **turn** is one `invoke_agent` span (one user request). Tokens and AI credits live on its child `chat <model>` runs.
- `src/lib/attribution` assigns each turn to project, team, issue and PR with a confidence level: manual > branch > PR head branch > commit > inferred > project only.
- `src/lib/cost` computes three views: AI credits (`copilot_usage_nano_aiu / 1e9`, 1 credit = $0.01), API-equivalent cost (tokens x list price) and subscription cost (seat + overage).
- `src/lib/report` aggregates rows for the pages in `src/app`.
## Conventions
- Name branches `feat/<issue>-slug` or `fix/<issue>-slug` so cost is attributed to the issue exactly.
- Never edit `src/lib/types.ts` without updating every consumer.
- Missing data is `null`, never `0` (for example a turn without credits shows "no data").
- Next.js 16 with `cacheComponents`: pages read the DB inside `<Suspense>` after `connection()`.
## How to answer
- Cite the file and function you used.
- Keep answers short: 3 to 6 sentences unless asked for more.
- Do not run `npm run seed`: it wipes the real synced data.
## Checks
`npx vitest run`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint src scripts`.
